app.name: ServiceNow Platform REST API (per-instance OAuth client)

verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you must register a client record on each ServiceNow instance you connect to. That takes minutes and needs no ServiceNow review, but listing an app on the ServiceNow Store is a separate, partner-gated process with certification.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a per-instance client; add a day or two if you must wait for a developer instance; days to weeks of work for Store certification
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 min once you have an instance you administer (a developer instance request can add a day or two)
verdict.approval_wait: None found for a per-instance registry client (inferred). Store certification: 3-5 weeks per ServiceNow's 2023 guidance, not a confirmed current figure.

gates.name: Your own instance (developer or admin-created client)
gates.unlocks: You create an OAuth registry record on an instance you administer and connect your own account through Composio.
limits: Access token lifetime defaults to 30 minutes; refresh token defaults to 100 days and can be increased on the record (f5).
A refresh token is returned only if Refresh Token Lifespan is greater than zero (f6).
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes, plus waitlist time if you request a developer instance

gates.name: Other users on the same instance (per-instance client)
gates.unlocks: Other users and admins of that customer instance can authorize the same registry client. Store listing is not needed.
limits: No install cap, rate limit or warning screen for unreviewed OAuth clients was documented (inferred from absence of findings).
Access is governed by each user's roles and ACLs; the default useraccount scope carries the full user-profile permissions (f11, f12).
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1 once the instance admin creates the record

gates.name: ServiceNow Store listing (certified app)
gates.unlocks: Listing a packaged app on the ServiceNow Store so any ServiceNow customer can install it from the Store.
limits: Only a Build Partner can list on the Store (f20).
Technology Partner Program membership is required to sell certified apps (f21). Current fee unconfirmed.
Publishing is only from a vendor instance, not a PDI (f22, f23).
Code changes after certification require re-submission (f31).
gates.time_to_reach: 3-5 weeks after design is complete, per ServiceNow's 2023 guidance; can be longer, and partner enrollment must come first

steps.title: Get an instance you administer
steps.detail: Use a developer instance (PDI) from the ServiceNow developer site, or a sub-production/production instance where you hold the admin role. Requesting a PDI puts you on a waitlist that can take a day or two. The developer site needs JavaScript and a supported browser.
steps.est_time: 10 min active; 1-2 days waiting if requesting a PDI
gotchas: Confirm the instance hostname (https://{instance}.service-now.com). Composio uses it as the subdomain.

steps.title: Confirm the OAuth 2.0 plugin is active
steps.detail: As an admin, check that the system property com.snc.platform.security.oauth.is.active is set to true. Without it the instance will not generate tokens.
gotchas: The plugin is active by default on new and upgraded instances, so this is usually a check, not a change.

steps.title: Create the registry record
steps.detail: Go to System OAuth > Application Registry, click New, then choose Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients. Enter a Name for the client. Leave Client Secret blank to have the instance generate one.

values.label: Menu path
values.value: System OAuth > Application Registry > New > Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients

values.label: Name
values.value: Any name you will recognise, e.g. your agent or product name

gotchas: Client ID and Client Secret are generated by the instance, not by you (f4).

steps.title: Set the Redirect URL and scope
steps.detail: Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config into the Redirect URL field. Set Auth scope to useraccount, which is the default scope Composio requests. Set Refresh Token Lifespan above zero so a refresh token is issued.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URL must match the Composio callback exactly, or the authorization will fail.
Whether Composio's callback host is accepted as a Redirect URL on a customer instance has not been verified against a live instance. Test in Step 7.
A Redirect URL of blank or 0 refresh lifespan means no refresh token is returned (f6).

steps.title: Save and copy the credentials
steps.detail: Click Submit to save the record. Open it again and copy the Client ID and Client Secret into a secrets manager. Do not commit them to source control.
gotchas: Leave the Active checkbox on, or the client will not be usable.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in Composio
steps.detail: In your Composio auth config for the servicenow toolkit, enter your instance subdomain, Client ID and Client Secret. Composio builds the authorize and token URLs from the subdomain. Keep the default scope useraccount.
gotchas: Composio has no managed app for ServiceNow, so an auth config without your own client ID will not work.

steps.title: Test the connection with your own account
steps.detail: Connect your own ServiceNow user through the Composio flow and confirm a token is returned with a refresh token. Then make one read-only API call. An agent can draft the test script, but you must run the authorization as a user.
gotchas: Token requests must be URL-encoded POST bodies (f15).
If no refresh token appears, check Refresh Token Lifespan is above zero (f6).

steps.title: Decide on the grant type (optional client-credentials path)
steps.detail: The flow above uses the authorization-code grant. On Washington DC and later, you can instead use client credentials for a service account: set glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled to true, then create the record and populate the OAuth Application User with a permissioned user. Do not mark the record as a public client.
gotchas: Under client credentials the Redirect URL and Login URL are not used (f10).
The token has no scopes until scopes are assigned; access depends on the OAuth Application User's roles and ACLs (f12).
Composio's stock flow may not support this grant. Confirm with Composio before relying on it.

steps.title: Set scope and permissions deliberately
steps.detail: useraccount gives the full set of permissions of the authorizing user. If you need narrower access, use ServiceNow API Authentication Scopes to bind the client to specific APIs, and limit the user's roles. An agent can draft the scope justification you give to the instance admin.
gotchas: Community guidance says that adding an Auth Scopes row can turn broad scoping into a strict allow-list that breaks access on some releases. Test after each change (f13).
Scope guidance comes from a third-party source on Zurich-era releases; verify on your release.

steps.title: Share with users on the same instance
steps.detail: Other users or admins on the same instance can authorize the same registry client through Composio. No ServiceNow review is required for this, and no install cap was found. Confirm the instance admin has approved the record and roles for each user group.
gotchas: Expect token refresh every 30 minutes for access tokens unless you rely on the refresh token (f5).

steps.title: Check whether Store listing is needed
steps.detail: Skip this step if the app is only for your own customers' instances. If you want a public Store listing, you need Build Partner status (Partner Program), Technology Partner membership, and a vendor instance. A PDI cannot publish to the Store. The app must be a scoped application.
steps.est_time: Weeks to months, depending on partner enrollment
gotchas: Global-scope apps cannot be published to the Store (f32).
The current Technology Partner fee is unconfirmed; an older $5,000 figure exists but a 2026 release says a single annual fee now applies (f33, f34).

steps.title: Prepare the Store package
steps.detail: An agent can draft the design document, test plan, customer-facing installation guide and listing copy for the certification team. You must run the Certification Self-Test Tool on the submitted version using the Validate Application button on the app record in the vendor instance.

values.label: Self-Test
values.value: Validate Application button on the app record (vendor instance)

gotchas: Common failures: UI actions with an empty condition, missing ACLs on tables and client-callable script includes, unsafe Jelly, missing contact support module (2023 list, may be outdated).

steps.title: Publish and submit for certification
steps.detail: From the vendor instance, use Publish to ServiceNow Store on the app record to upload a copy. Then submit App Review and Listing Review from the Certify page in the Store Publisher Portal. Questions go to the ServiceNow certification team by email.
gotchas: App Review covers security, performance, stability, installation and architecture; Listing Review covers accuracy and branding, including demo videos.
Requirements sit in a knowledge base behind a portal login.

steps.title: Wait for certification
steps.detail: ServiceNow's 2023 guidance says design-complete to ready-to-publish typically takes 3-5 weeks. Expect days to longer than five weeks, and more iteration if the app is large.
gotchas: Any code change after certification requires re-submission for app and listing re-certification (f31).

requirements.item: Instance with the OAuth 2.0 plugin active and com.snc.platform.security.oauth.is.active = true
requirements.detail: Needed before any token can be generated on the instance.

requirements.item: Registry record created by an instance admin (System OAuth > Application Registry)
requirements.detail: Client ID and Client Secret are generated by the instance.

requirements.item: Redirect URL on the record matches the Composio callback exactly
requirements.detail: Mismatch blocks authorization. Live matching is unverified (see open questions).

requirements.item: Refresh Token Lifespan greater than 0 for refresh tokens
requirements.detail: Default is 100 days; no refresh token is returned at zero.

requirements.item: Public Client not checked for confidential clients
requirements.detail: Applies to the client-credentials grant; confirm for the grant you use.

requirements.item: Scoped app required for Store publishing
requirements.detail: Global-scope apps cannot be listed on the Store.

requirements.item: Build Partner status required to list on the Store
requirements.detail: Joining the ServiceNow Partner Program is the route.

requirements.item: Technology Partner Program membership to sell certified apps
requirements.detail: Membership gives vendor instances. Fee amount unconfirmed.

requirements.item: Publishing only from a vendor instance, not a PDI
requirements.detail: A PDI cannot publish to the Store.

requirements.item: Certification Self-Test run on the submitted version
requirements.detail: Use the Validate Application button on the app record.

requirements.item: Design document, test plan with results, and customer-facing installation guide

requirements.detail: Any change after certification needs re-submission.

scopes.effect: Composio default. Grants the full set of permissions of the authorizing user profile, so it is broad. Access is still limited by the user's roles and ACLs. ServiceNow does not describe tiers for it, so no review tier applies. Narrow with API Authentication Scopes if needed.

blockers.cause: Refresh Token Lifespan on the registry record is zero or blank, so no refresh token is issued.
blockers.fix: Set Refresh Token Lifespan above zero (default 100 days) and reconnect.

blockers.symptom: API calls with a valid token fail with permission errors, or the token has no scopes
blockers.cause: Under client credentials the token has no scopes until scopes are assigned, and access depends on the OAuth Application User's roles and ACLs. Scope rows can also turn into a strict allow-list.
blockers.fix: Assign the OAuth Application User the needed roles. Check Auth Scopes on the record and remove rows that are not intended. Retest after each change.

blockers.symptom: Cannot publish the app to the ServiceNow Store from a PDI
blockers.cause: Store publishing is allowed only from a vendor instance; a PDI is for learning and proof-of-concept only.
blockers.fix: Build in a vendor instance from Technology Partner Program membership.

blockers.symptom: Cannot list the app on the ServiceNow Store
blockers.cause: Only a Build Partner can list an application on the Store.
blockers.fix: Join the ServiceNow Partner Program and reach Build Partner status first.

blockers.symptom: Store app rejected for global scope
blockers.cause: Global-scope applications cannot be published to the Store.
blockers.fix: Build the app as a scoped application before submission.

blockers.symptom: Certification rejection, e.g. unconditioned UI actions or missing ACLs
blockers.cause: Common failures in the 2023 top-ten list include UI actions with an empty condition, missing ACLs on tables and client-callable script includes, unsafe Jelly, and a missing contact support module.
blockers.fix: Run the Self-Test tool, fix flagged items, and retest before submitting. Email the certification team with specific questions.
blockers.contact: ServiceNow certification team (email; address in Store Publisher Portal)

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you must supply your own client ID and secret from a registry record on the target instance. Its redirect URL must match the Redirect URL on that record. Per-instance clients need no ServiceNow store or partner approval; only the instance admin creates one. Store certification only matters if you want a public Store listing.

open_questions: Official docs.servicenow.com pages for the Application Registry were not fetched. Registry steps rely on community posts, a ServiceNow-employee developer blog and partner guides. Confirm the field labels against your release's docs.
Whether a Composio callback URL is accepted as a Redirect URL on a customer instance has not been verified against a live instance. Test in the Composio flow before relying on it.
Per-instance OIDC discovery and live authorize behaviour on a real customer instance could not be probed; only developer.service-now.com was reachable and it redirects to developer.servicenow.com.
Whether ServiceNow requires any review before a third-party client receives a client ID on an instance is not confirmed by an official page. None was found; the instance admin creates the record.
Whether Composio supports the client-credentials grant for ServiceNow is unknown. The authorization-code flow is the assumed default.
Current Technology Partner membership fee: $5,000 is from an older guide. The 2026 newsroom confirms a single annual fee but not the amount.
Certification timeline: 3-5 weeks is from a 2023 ServiceNow post. A third-party source gives 5-8 weeks end to end, which is not repeated here as fact.
Install caps or rate limits for unreviewed OAuth clients or Store apps: none found.
The full certification requirements (KB0030070) sit behind a Store Publisher Portal login and could not be read. Rejection reasons come from a 2023 post and may be outdated.
The grant types listed in the 2020 blog may be out of date. The current supported grant list on the latest release was not confirmed.
